body:
### Motivation
- Introduce smart/automatic playlists driven by playback history and surface them in the main menu. 
- Provide several smart queries (most played, recently discovered, not played since X, night/top, study mode) to power those playlists. 
- Make the home/menu UI more responsive and adjust hero/category card sizing for different screen orientations. 
- Store additional playback metadata (`played_ms`, `source`) and increment the database schema version for the new features.

### Description
- Added two new screens: `SmartPlaylistsScreen` and `UnheardIn30DaysScreen` under `views/smartplaylists` and integrated navigation routes for `SmartPlaylists` and `UnheardIn30Days` in `NavController.kt`.
- Extended `PlaybackHistoryDao` with multiple smart playlist queries (`getMostPlayedSince`, `getRecentlyDiscovered`, `getNotPlayedSince`, `getTopNightTracks`, `getStudyModeTracks`) and added a `SmartPlaylistTrack` data class to receive those query projections.
- Updated the `PlaybackHistory` entity to include `played_ms` and `source` fields, and bumped the Room DB version from `3` to `4` in `PulsePlayerDatabase.kt` while preserving the existing `fallbackToDestructiveMigration` behavior and enabling foreign keys on open.
- Refactored `menu.kt` to add smart playlist entries, make the layout responsive using `BoxWithConstraints`, compute dynamic column counts and card heights, add vertical scrolling, and pass compact sizing into `HeroMusicCard` and `CategoryCard` (plus alias route imports to avoid naming collisions).

### Testing

author: copilot
body:
Bare `except:` clauses in `GRGObject.__getitem__` and `__setitem__` were catching all exceptions—including unexpected ones from property getters/setters—and re-raising them as `KeyError`, masking the real error.

## Changes

- **`__getitem__` / `__setitem__`**: Replace bare `except:` with `except AttributeError:` so only missing-attribute lookups become `KeyError`; all other exceptions (e.g. `ValueError` from a setter) bubble up naturally.

```python
# Before: a ValueError raised inside a setter would silently become KeyError
obj["some_prop"] = bad_value  # raises KeyError('Invalid key: some_prop') — wrong

# After: the real exception propagates
obj["some_prop"] = bad_value  # raises ValueError from the setter — correct
```

body:
Thanks for asking me to work on this. I will get started on it and keep this PR's description up to date as I form a plan and make progress.

> 1) Read docs and README.
> 
> TRIAD AI PROTOCOL — 100-POINT PLAN (COMMUNICATION, GOALS, RESTRAINTS)
> Applies to: Dr. Eams (user-facing), IDARi (admin/optimizer), Boogie (policy/overwatch).
> Goal: Make the three agents behave like a single coherent system: safe, fast, explainable, non-spaghetti, no contradictory actions.
> 
> 2) Define the triad as three roles with zero overlap ambiguity:
>    - Dr. Eams = conversation + guidance + UX explanations + user assistance.
>    - IDARi = bug fixer + performance optimizer + compressor + admin tooling.
>    - Boogie = policy enforcement + abuse detection + restriction/ban logic.
> 3) Store these role definitions in a single doc: `docs/AI_TRIAD_PROTOCOL.md` (source of truth).
> 4) Publish a short public version: `docs/POLICY_TRIAD_OVERVIEW.md` and expose at `/policy/ai`.
> 5) Add a README link to `/policy/ai` so users can read what each AI does.
> 
> 6) Establish a single shared “event bus” concept: all inter-agent communication happens via typed events.
> 7) Define a canonical event schema (TypeScript types) in `lib/ai/events.ts`.
> 8) Every event MUST include: `event_id`, `timestamp`, `actor`, `target`, `type`, `severity`, `user_id?`, `dream_id?`, `context_refs[]`, `policy_version?`.
> 9) Add `correlation_id` so multiple events in one incident can be traced end-to-end.
> 10) Require all agents to attach `policy_version` when the event relates to enforcement or user restrictions.
> 
> 11) Define the allowed message types between agents:
>     - `REQUEST_REVIEW`
>     - `REQUEST_EXPLANATION`
>     - `REQUEST_OPTIMIZATION`
>     - `INCIDENT_DETECTED`
>     - `ACTION_TAKEN`
>     - `SUGGESTION_PROPOSED`
>     - `SUGGESTION_APPROVED`
>     - `SUGGESTION_REJECTED`
>     - `STATUS_SNAPSHOT`
>     - `APPEAL_RECEIVED`
> 12) Define a single ingestion point for events (server-side) so clients can’t spoof triad traffic.
> 13) Log all triad events into an audit table (Supabase) with role-based access.
> 14) Expose user-safe subsets of events for UI (“why did this happen?”) via Dr. Eams only.
> 15) Never expose raw triad event logs publicly; public docs describe behavior, not internal telemetry.
> 
> 16) Define the triad’s primary system goals:
>     - Safety & compliance (Boogie)
>     - Reliability & performance (IDARi)
>     - User clarity & productivity (Dr. Eams)
> 17) Add a single overarching product goal: “Premium, iOS-natural interface that remains safe and fast under growth.”
> 18) Add a single operational goal: “No silent failures; every issue results in a visible state + next step.”
> 19) Add a single trust goal: “Users can understand what happened without seeing sensitive detection details.”
> 20) Add a single engineering goal: “No spaghetti; changes must be typed, versioned, documented.”
> 
> 21) Establish hard restraints for each agent:
>     - Dr. Eams: cannot enforce, ban, or change policy thresholds.
>     - IDARi: cannot ban users or override Boogie; cannot change public policy text alone.
>     - Boogie: cannot optimize performance; cannot make product UX decisions; cannot deploy code changes alone.
> 22) Enforce these restraints in code by permission checks (role-based server guard).
> 23) Require explicit admin authorization to run high-impact actions (perma-ban, global setting changes).
> 24) Require triad unanimity for major system updates (see governance below).
> 25) Add “blast radius” classification for all actions: `LOCAL`, `USER`, `SYSTEM`, `GLOBAL`.
> 
> 26) Define a governance handshake for major updates:
>     - Proposal created (any agent)
>     - Triad review (all three respond)
>     - Unanimous approval required
>     - Human/admin confirmation required for GLOBAL changes
> 27) Define “major update” as: policy changes, auth flows, monetization, connector permissions, public data exposure.
> 28) Define “minor update” as: UI polish, non-breaking perf improvements, bug fixes with tests.
> 29) For minor updates: IDARi can proceed but must notify Boogie and Dr. Eams via `STATUS_SNAPSHOT`.
> 30) For enforcement changes: Boogie leads but must notify Dr. Eams for messaging copy and IDARi for performance impact.
> 
> 31) Define incident handling flow (the triad’s “immune response”):
>     - Detect incident (Boogie or IDARi)
>     - Contain (Boogie actions or IDARi throttles)
>     - Explain (Dr. Eams)
>     - Recover (IDARi)
>     - Learn (triad update proposal)
> 32) Boogie is authoritative for safety actions during an incident.
> 33) IDARi is authoritative for system throttling/perf degradation handling during an incident.
> 34) Dr. Eams is authoritative for user communication during an incident.
> 35) If a user asks Dr. Eams “why am I restricted?”, Dr. Eams must query Boogie’s event summary and relay it.
> 
> 36) Define conflict resolution:
>     - If Boogie says “restrict”, restriction happens.
>     - If IDARi says “system is overloaded”, system throttles happen.
>     - If Dr. Eams disagrees on messaging tone, it can adjust copy but not reverse action.
> 37) If Boogie’s confidence is low, Boogie must choose lesser restrictions and escalate.
> 38) If IDARi proposes changes that affect policy surfaces, it must send `REQUEST_REVIEW` to Boogie.
> 39) If Dr. Eams proposes a UX change that impacts enforcement surfaces, it must send `REQUEST_REVIEW` to Boogie.
> 40) If any agent detects potential false positives, it must trigger `REQUEST_REVIEW` to Boogie.
> 
> 41) Define a single set of shared platform limits all agents respect:
>     - max dreams/widgets (e.g., 48 default)
>     - refresh/data budgets
>     - rate limits for posting/sharing/messaging
>     - connector permissions
> 42) Boogie enforces user behavior rate limits.
> 43) IDARi enforces system health rate limits (load shedding) independent of user punishment.
> 44) Dr. Eams explains rate limits as product constraints, not punishments, unless Boogie flagged enforcement.
> 45) Keep “system throttling” clearly separate from “policy punishment” in UI.
> 
> 46) Define the shared terminology dictionary:
>     - Dreams = user-installed widgets/apps
>     - Daydreams = 6 specialized first-party experiences
>     - Home/Profile = core dreams
>     - Share Code = config-only blueprint
> 47) Put the dictionary in `docs/TERMS.md` and require all agents to use it.
> 48) Require PRs to update TERMS.md if new public vocabulary is introduced.
> 49) Require Dr. Eams to mirror the exact vocabulary in user messages.
> 50) Require Boogie to reference rule codes that match public policy wording.
> 
> 51) Define what each agent communicates to the others:
>     - Boogie → Dr. Eams: restriction state, reason codes, durations, appeal links.
>     - Boogie → IDARi: abuse telemetry, spam patterns, suggested throttle knobs.
>     - IDARi → Boogie: system anomalies that look like abuse vs outages; false-positive suspicion.
>     - IDARi → Dr. Eams: system degradation state; recommended user guidance.
>     - Dr. Eams → Boogie: user appeal requests, contextual clarifications, misunderstandings.
>     - Dr. Eams → IDARi: user-reported bugs, UX friction clusters.
> 52) All agent-to-agent messages must be emitted as typed events, not direct chat text.
> 53) Every event must be idempotent (safe to reprocess without duplication).
> 54) Every event must be stored with an immutable record.
> 55) Provide an admin console view to see correlated incident timelines.
> 
> 56) Define user communication constraints:
>     - Only Dr. Eams speaks to users in natural language.
>     - Boogie and IDARi output structured data for UI and for Dr. Eams.
> 57) Boogie’s user-facing content must be short templates, not freeform text.
> 58) IDARi’s user-facing content must be “system status” messages, not blame.
> 59) Dr. Eams must never claim the system did something it didn’t do; it must cite event summaries.

### Motivation
- Make geocoding failure cases explicit and handle fallbacks robustly.
- Return richer search results (top 5) with selectable units and damage-path corridor geometry for improved UX and sharing.
- Modernize the web UI to present multiple results, sharing links, and corridor visualization.

### Description
- Introduced `GeocodingError`, `NoGeocodeMatchError`, and `GeocoderUnavailableError` in `geocode.py` and updated `_geocode_census`/`_geocode_nominatim` to raise them and `geocode_oneline` to fall back appropriately.

- Updated `schemas.py` to include `selected_unit`, `selected_distance`, optional `corridor_geojson`, `top_results`, and `share_url`, and normalized request validation in `ClosestTornadoRequest`.
- Redesigned the frontend in `web.py` with a modern UI, support for selecting among the top 5 results, sharing via privacy-safe coordinate links, and rendering of corridor/track/closest/user layers on the map.
- Added unit tests under `tests/` for guardrails, import utilities, main endpoints (including mocked DB and geocoding), and schema validation.
- Bumped API `version` in `FastAPI` app metadata and adjusted cache keys to include `units` and a versioned namespace.

### Testing
- Ran the new unit tests in `tests/` (`test_guardrails.py`, `test_import_utils.py`, `test_main_endpoint.py`, `test_schemas.py`) using the repository test runner; all tests passed.
- Exercised HTTP paths with `TestClient` in `test_main_endpoint.py` including `/closest-tornado` and `/closest-tornado-by-coords` with mocked DB and geocoder, and those assertions succeeded.

author: copilot
body:
As `runs.json` and `repos.json` grow over time, passing their contents via `$(cat file)` shell substitution into `--argjson` exceeds the OS argument list size limit (~2MB), causing jq to exit 126.

## Changes

- **Replace `--argjson "$(cat file)"` with `--slurpfile file`** — jq reads files directly, bypassing the shell argument list entirely
- **Save existing `repos-summary.json` to a temp file** — pass it as jq's positional input instead of piping via `echo "$EXISTING"` variable expansion
- **Update jq filter** — use `$runs[0]` / `$repos[0]` since `--slurpfile` wraps parsed JSON in an outer array

```bash
# Before (breaks when files grow large)
echo "$EXISTING" | jq \
  --argjson runs "$(cat /tmp/runs.json)" \
  --argjson repos "$(cat /tmp/repos.json)" \
  '...$runs[]...$repos[]...' > repos-summary.json

# After
jq \
  --slurpfile runs /tmp/runs.json \
  --slurpfile repos /tmp/repos.json \
  '...$runs[0][]...$repos[0][]...' /tmp/existing-summary.json > repos-summary.json
```

## Summary

Updates the CE gem to commit `03f673e1` which includes the `fix(mcp): reconstruct request from headers in PunditIntegration` fix from PR #1263 in community-engine-rails.

## Problem

`FastMcp::Tool` tools are initialized with `@headers` (the full Rack env hash) but have no `#request` method. `PunditIntegration#request` was calling `super` which always raised `NoMethodError`. This caused all `tools/call` MCP requests to fail with 500 errors.

## Fix

`PunditIntegration#request` now reconstructs an `ActionDispatch::Request` from the stored `@headers`, making Pundit authorization work correctly for all MCP tool calls.

## Also fixes

Pre-existing rubocop offenses on `main` that were causing CI to fail:
- `config/initializers/asset_sync.rb`: `ENV.fetch` with default nil

author: dhruvhaldar
body:
💡 **What**: Optimized the calculation of `f(a/W)` in `griffith/geometry.py`.
🎯 **Why**: Exponentiation operations (such as `x ** 1.5` or `x ** 2`) are inherently more expensive than single multiplications or native square root operations (`math.sqrt` or `np.sqrt`). By replacing `(1 - alpha) ** 1.5` with `(1 - alpha) * math.sqrt(1 - alpha)` and `alpha ** 2` with `alpha * alpha`, and caching `(1 - alpha)` as `one_minus_alpha`, we reduce computational overhead.
📊 **Impact**: This micro-optimization speeds up this function by ~40% (for both scalar `math` and array `numpy` paths), which is critical since it is likely evaluated frequently in iterative root-finding methods or matrix calculations. 
🔬 **Measurement**: Verified with the existing unit test suite, and used local `timeit` benchmarks to validate the performance improvement.

author: copilot
body:
Some manga sources split pages into a main page and a thin bottom strip ("stub"), causing the stub to appear as a separate page when swiping. This adds a **Smart page combine** option in pager viewer settings that automatically detects and merges such stubs into the preceding page.

### Detection heuristic (`ImageUtil`)
- `isSmallPage()`: stub if next page width is within ±5% of current page and height < 30% of current page height
- `mergePages()`: vertically stacks two `BufferedSource` images; uses `max()` of widths for the canvas

### Pager integration
- `PagerPageHolder.trySmartCombine()`: called from `process()` when dual-page split is inactive or page is not wide; fetches next page stream (only if `Page.State.Ready`), checks stub heuristic, merges, then triggers `onPageAbsorb()`
- `PagerViewer.onPageAbsorb()` → `PagerViewerAdapter.onPageAbsorb()`: removes the absorbed stub from the item list on the UI thread (mirrors the existing `onPageSplit` pattern)

### Settings
- New `smartCombinePaged()` boolean preference (default off), wired through `ViewerConfig.smartCombine` and `PagerConfig`
- Checkbox added to **Pager viewer** section of the reader settings sheet

body: # Fix: Add tracking admin module to production panel + vessel autocomplete ## Summary The tracking admin module (`tracking-admin.js`) was only loaded in the test admin panel (`panel-test/admin/index.html`) but **not** in the production admin panel (`panel/admin/index.html`). This is why creating a vessel from the admin panel didn't result in a trackable vessel — the tracking module wasn't loaded at all in production. **Changes:** 1. **Added `tracking-admin.js` script tag** to `panel/admin/index.html` (the root cause fix) 2. **Added `tracking-admin.js` file** to `panel/admin/assets/` (copied from panel-test, with enhancements) 3. **New API endpoint `admin_lookup_vessel`** in `tracking_api.php` — searches local DB by name/IMO/MMSI/callsign, falls back to VesselFinder API for exact IMO (7-digit) or MMSI (9-digit) lookups 4. **Autocomplete in "Crear Embarcacion" form** — typing in the Name field triggers a debounced lookup against local DB; entering a complete IMO or MMSI auto-fills the rest of the form ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Verify the tracking module loads in production admin panel** — navigate to `/panel/admin/#tracking` and confirm the "Tracking" sidebar item appears and the vessel list renders - [ ] **Test vessel creation end-to-end** — create a vessel from admin, then check it appears in the user panel's "Seguimiento" section (requires `is_featured` checked) - [ ] **Test autocomplete** — open "Crear Embarcacion", type a known vessel name or IMO, verify the dropdown appears and selecting an item fills the form fields - [ ] **Check for listener leaks** — open and close the create modal multiple times; verify no duplicate dropdowns or performance degradation (the `document.addEventListener("click")` for closing the dropdown is added each time the modal opens and is never removed) - [ ] **Verify SQL safety** — the `adminLookupVessel` endpoint uses LIKE queries with parameterized bindings, but confirm no injection vectors exist with the `$query` parameter ### Notes - The VesselFinder external API lookup only fires for exact 7-digit IMO or 9-digit MMSI queries, and only when there are zero local DB results. Name-based search is local-only. - The `fillFormFromResult` function only sets fields when the value is truthy — empty strings from VesselFinder (e.g. `shipping_line: ''`) won't overwrite previously entered data, which could be confusing if the user selects a different result after partially filling the form. - Recommended test plan: deploy to the test environment first (`panel-test`), create a vessel with autocomplete, verify it shows in the user panel, then promote to production. Link to Devin run: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/90c479848fc74cf08980a36d2170879f Requested by: @jpchs1 ---

author: exponentialr
body:
## Summary
This PR adds a deterministic v2 synthetic data generator, a regional name pool, and full data-pack contract documentation for Financescr.  
It also adds automated tests for generator outputs and fixes a determinism bug in name variant generation.

## Why
- Improve realism and reproducibility of synthetic fincrime/credit data.
- Make `/data` pack schemas explicit and easier to validate.
- Prevent silent drift in generated fixtures.

## Changes

### Data generation
- Added `scripts/generate_data_v2.py`
  - Generates versioned `fincrime`, `credit`, and `golden` packs.
  - Uses seeded deterministic generation.
  - Adds optional raw credit fields and derived features (`credit_utilisation`, `bank_balance_volatility`).
- Added `scripts/names_v1.json`
  - Weighted regional first/last-name pools + alias/transliteration support.

### Determinism fix
- Updated name variant construction in `generate_data_v2.py` to use ordered deduping (list + seen set) instead of unordered set iteration.
- This removes cross-process hash-order nondeterminism in outputs (notably `watchlist.jsonl`).

### Documentation
- Rewrote `README.md` with:
  - Local setup and external data-pack mount flow
  - Detailed fincrime/credit/golden schemas
  - API usage and roadmap
- Updated `.gitignore` to ignore `tasks.md`.

### Tests
- Added `tests/test_generate_data_v2.py`:
  - Smoke test for expected files and row counts
  - Determinism test (same seed => identical file hashes)
  - Credit derived-feature invariant test from raw fields (with tight numeric tolerance)

## Impact
- No API contract changes in this PR.
- Adds new generator/test assets and data-contract documentation.
- Improves reliability of generated fixtures for downstream evaluation.

## Validation
- Ran full test suite:
  - `.venv/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py' -v`
  - Result: `33` tests passed.

## Risks / Notes
- README is now much more detailed; keep docs aligned with implementation in follow-up PRs.
- Optional v2 raw credit fields may require relaxed schema handling in strict downstream consumers.

body:
💡 **What**: Optimized the keyword matching logic in the `getPortfolio` tool inside `src/tools/trading.ts`. Replaced the manual keyword array iteration that used `.some()` and `.toLowerCase()` with a single pre-compiled case-insensitive regular expression (`PORTFOLIO_REGEX`).

🎯 **Why**: The original implementation allocated new lowercase strings and iterated through a 10-item keyword array for every single line in the snapshot text (which could be quite large). This O(lines * keywords) operation was a performance bottleneck.

📊 **Impact**: Reduces CPU overhead and memory allocations during text parsing. Benchmarks indicate a ~66% performance improvement (~280ms down to ~94ms for processing 10000 lines).

🔬 **Measurement**: Created a standalone benchmarking script (`bench_logic.ts`) that runs both versions of the logic on 10000 dummy lines. The script output confirms the performance improvement while maintaining 100% logic parity.

author: copilot
body:
Silent failure modes in `setup.sh`, `build.sh`, and `verify-install.sh` made debugging installation and build problems difficult. Broken venvs went undetected, `cd` in build functions permanently mutated the process working directory, and errors from pip/venv were swallowed.

## `scripts/setup.sh`
- Detect broken venv (dir exists, binary missing) → delete and recreate before proceeding
- Capture stderr from both primary and `--without-pip` fallback venv creation; surface on failure

Backport 1/1 commits from #164559.

Newer Docker versions (as shipped with Ubuntu 24.04) create OCI image indexes even for single-architecture builds. `docker manifest create` refuses to accept a manifest list as a source, causing failures like:

  us-docker.pkg.dev/.../cockroach:amd64-v26.1.0-rc.1-... is a manifest list

Add a `create_and_push_multi_arch_manifest` helper to teamcity-support.sh that uses `docker buildx imagetools create`, which handles both plain manifests and OCI image indexes as sources. Falls back to the old `docker manifest create` flow if buildx is unavailable.

Update all release scripts to use the new helper. In publish-staged-cockroach-release.sh, also drop GCR latest/latest-branch manifests that were created but never pushed (dead code), and restructure DockerHub latest/latest-branch creation to only happen when the manifest will actually be pushed, since buildx imagetools create pushes immediately.

This PR adds a new `crypto/` skill category with the **FUD Analyzer** tool.

Measures what percentage of someone's Twitter/X activity is **FUD** (Fear, Uncertainty, Doubt) toward crypto projects vs shilling.

## Problem
The sitemap was using **hash-fragment URLs** (`/#stats`, `/#create`, `/#manage`, `/#docs`) which Google **cannot index** — hash fragments are never sent to the server and are invisible to crawlers.

This means Google was only indexing 2 of your 7 pages (homepage and privacy policy).

- Added `interstitial.html` to the sitemap
- Updated all `lastmod` dates to current

## Impact
This should improve SEO indexing and may help with AdSense approval, since Google will now see multiple content-rich pages instead of just one.

author: giulio-leone
body:
## Problem

`RunnableSequence.batch()` and `abatch()` use `list.pop(0)` to reassemble outputs by merging a `failed_inputs_map` with remaining successful inputs consumed front-to-back.

`list.pop(0)` is **O(n)** per call because CPython must shift every remaining element. For large batch sizes this accumulates to **O(n²)** total work.

## Solution

Convert the copied inputs list to a `collections.deque` and replace `.pop(0)` with `.popleft()`, which is **O(1)** amortised. The `collections` module is already imported in this file.

## Testing

All 6 batch-related tests pass:
- `test_retry_batch_preserves_order`
- `test_async_retry_batch_preserves_order`
- `test_seq_batch_return_exceptions`
- `test_seq_abatch_return_exceptions`
- `test_runnable_branch_batch`
- `test_runnable_branch_abatch`

(2 consecutive clean runs)

The PR fixes a race condition when concurrent writes during block trimming causes WAL corruption. In short, the blocks are trimmed after being re-used by another transaction.

`WriteHeader()` adds freed blocks to `free_list` and `fully_freed_blocks` under the lock, then releases the lock before `TrimFreeBlocks()` runs. A concurrent writer could allocate one of those blocks, write data to it, and commit a WAL entry referencing it. `TrimFreeBlocks()` would then zero the live block, causing a checksum mismatch on WAL replay after restart:

```
Query failed with message: IO Error: Corrupt database file: computed checksum 5381 does not match stored checksum 0 in block at location 274432
```

Fix: re-acquire the lock in `TrimFreeBlocks()` before zeroing each block and skip any block no longer in `free_list` (i.e. concurrently allocated).

Add a regression test using `TrimRaceFileSystem`, which intercepts `Trim()` before the zeroing occurs, runs a racing writer that allocates the block from `free_list` and commits, then lets `Trim()` proceed. Phase 2 reopens the database and replays the WAL: without the fix it fails with a checksum mismatch; with the fix it succeeds.

body:
## Summary

Closes #200

- Add `tileops/kernels/online_softmax.py` with shared `LOG2E` constant and macro-generating utilities (`make_log2e_scale`, `make_online_softmax`, `make_rescale`)
- Replace all 18 occurrences of the magic constant `1.44269504` with the shared `LOG2E` constant
- Replace duplicated online softmax blocks across 14 kernel files with calls to shared macros where the pattern matches exactly
- Keep custom softmax code in files with special patterns (infinity guards, extra `T.max` steps) while still using the shared `LOG2E` constant

## Details

### New shared module: `tileops/kernels/online_softmax.py`

| Utility | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `LOG2E` | Shared `log2(e)` constant (`1.44269504`) |
| `make_log2e_scale(dim)` | Returns `(1/sqrt(dim)) * LOG2E` |
| `make_online_softmax(scale, accum_dtype, block_rows, block_cols)` | Returns a `T.macro` that performs the full online softmax update step |
| `make_rescale(block_rows, head_dim)` | Returns a `T.macro` that rescales the output accumulator |

### Files using shared macros (full replacement)

- `flash_attn/fwd.py` — all 4 kernels (MHA/GQA × inline/pipelined)
- `flash_decode/mha_decode.py`, `gqa_decode.py`, `gqa_decode_paged.py` — both no-split and split paths
- `flash_decode/mha_decode_paged.py` — no-split path (split path has infinity guard)
- `deepseek_mla/deepseek_mla_decode.py` — both no-split and split paths
- `deepseek_nsa/nsa_fwd.py` — full macro replacement

### Files using shared LOG2E only (custom pattern preserved)

- `flash_attn/bwd.py` — uses pre-computed LSE (different algorithm)
- `flash_decode/mha_decode_paged.py` split path — has infinity guard
- `deepseek_mla/deepseek_dsa_decode.py` — complex infinity guard variations
- `deepseek_nsa/nsa_topk.py`, `nsa_cmp_fwd.py` — infinity guard patterns
- `deepseek_nsa/gqa_window_sliding.py` — extra `T.max` step
- `mhc/mhc_pre.py` — sigmoid/exp2 usage

## Test plan

- [x] All 14 modified files import successfully
- [x] Magic constant `1.44269504` only exists in single shared definition
- [x] `ruff check` passes clean on all modified files
- [x] CI tests pass

author: alexeyv
body:
## What

New reusable review task (`review-edge-case-hunter.xml`) that exhaustively traces branching paths and boundary conditions in code, reporting only unhandled gaps. Registered in `module-help.csv` as `bmad-review-edge-case-hunter`.

## Why

The existing adversarial review is attitude-driven (cynical persona). Pairing it with a method-driven reviewer that mechanically walks every path produces orthogonal findings with minimal overlap. This second perspective is proven useful but had no dedicated task definition.

## How

- Created `src/core/tasks/review-edge-case-hunter.xml` following the same XML task structure as the adversarial review
- Diff-scoped analysis: scans only diff hunks when a diff is provided, full content otherwise
- Structured JSON output with four fields: location, trigger_condition, guard_snippet, potential_consequence
- No persona — the forcing function is the exhaustive path-walk method, not an attitude
- Added registration row in `src/core/module-help.csv`

## Testing

- All existing tests pass (`npm test`)
- File reference validation confirms the new CSV row points to a valid file

### Motivation
- Provide a reproducible interop submission/aggregation workflow and CI guardrails for submission freshness and manifest validation. 
- Ship protocol-level operational alerting (`EXT-ALERTS`) and session resumption (`EXT-RESUME`) artifacts plus registries so alerts/resume semantics are machine-validateable and testable. 
- Deliver a deterministic behavioral enforcement demo (PASS + threat-driven EXPECTED_FAIL cases) to exercise mediated blocking, alerts, resume, and related conformance checks. 

### Description
- Add interop tooling and CI: new workflow `/.github/workflows/interop-matrix.yml`, tools `interop/tools/interop_matrix.py` and `interop/tools/validate_manifests.py`, schema `interop/schemas/implementation_manifest.schema.json`, templates and `interop/` docs and outputs. 
- Extend conformance harness and Makefile: new demo/profile/conformance targets in `Makefile`, conformance runner updates in `conformance/runner/aicp_conformance_runner.py` to validate `AL-` and `RS-` checks and add `ENF-AUTH-01`, and profile runner path formatting fix in `conformance/runner/aicp_profile_runner.py`. 
- Add EXT-ALERTS and EXT-RESUME RFCs, payload schemas, registry artifacts, message-type and extension-id registrations, and payload/schema files under `docs/`, `schemas/`, and `registry/`. 
- Add behavioral enforcement demo: generator script `demos/enforcement_behavioral/scripts/run_demo.py`, demo fixtures under `fixtures/demos/enforcement_behavioral/`, demo conformance suite `conformance/demos/DEMO_ENFORCEMENT_BEHAVIORAL_0.1.json`, results/history, rules, README, and helper demo tests.

author: rjchiba
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a portable, FastAPI-based IIIF Image API implementation that satisfies the requirements in `impl-plan-v0.1.md` and targets IIIF Image API 3.0 Level 1 as a baseline for interoperability. 
- Keep datastore integration pluggable by defining a connector contract so cloud-specific adapters (S3/GCS/OCI/etc.) can be added without changing the API surface. 

### Description
- Add a FastAPI application with routes for base redirect (`GET /iiif/{identifier}`), info document (`GET /iiif/{identifier}/info.json`), and canonical image requests (`GET /iiif/{identifier}/{region}/{size}/{rotation}/{quality}.{format}`) implemented in `app/main.py`. 
- Implement IIIF parameter parsing/validation and JPEG rendering using Pillow in `app/iiif.py`, supporting Level 1 features: `region` = `full`/`square`/`x,y,w,h`, `size` = `max`/`w,`/`,h`, `rotation` = `0`, `quality` = `default`, and `format` = `jpg`. 
- Define a connector contract `ImageSourceConnector` and provide a local filesystem connector `LocalFileConnector` in `app/connectors.py` to load source images while separating storage concerns. 
- Add packaging metadata (`pyproject.toml`), README updates documenting features and connector requirements, basic tests in `tests/test_app.py`, and a `.gitignore` to exclude `__pycache__` and `*.pyc`. 

### Testing
- Ran a bytecode validation with `python3 -m compileall app tests`, which succeeded. 
- Attempted to install dev dependencies with `python3 -m pip install -e .[dev]`, but installation failed due to network/proxy restrictions reaching PyPI. 
- Added unit tests in `tests/test_app.py` covering `info.json`, a full/max/default JPEG request, a Level 1 region+size request, and invalid rotation handling, but `pytest` was not executed because dependencies could not be installed in this environment.

### Motivation

- Prevent data-loss edge case where `clearAllData` could skip some `bearMathIslandBackup_` keys when deleting from `localStorage` while iterating.  
- Make tests reliable in a Node environment by providing a `localStorage` mock so storage logic can be validated without a browser.  
- Keep documentation accurate by aligning the `README` project-structure section with the repository layout and correcting a repository-name typo.

### Description

- Change `clearAllData` to first collect all keys that start with `bearMathIslandBackup_` into an array and then remove them, avoiding modification-during-iteration (applied in `src/utils/storage.ts` and mirrored in `src/utils/storage.js`).
- Add a `localStorage` in-memory mock and a regression test in `src/utils/storage.test.ts` that verifies all backup keys are removed while unrelated keys remain intact.  
- Update `README.md` to correct the repository name from `bear_math_island` to `bear-math-island` and simplify the `src/` project-structure entries to reflect actual files (`components`, `stores`, `utils`, `App.vue`, `main.ts`, `style.css`).

### Testing

- Ran the storage unit tests in Node environment with `npx vitest run --environment node src/utils/storage.test.ts`, and all tests passed (7 tests).  
- Ran a production build with `npm run build`, which completed successfully.

Adds the D&D 5e Systems Reference Document 5.2 (CC-BY-4.0) as a first-class structured ruleset option, giving session agents typed rule context (classes, skills, conditions, combat actions) rather than a freeform string.

## Description

**Backend — `server/agents/srd.py` (new)**
- `SRD_52_DATA`: structured SRD 5.2 content — 13 classes (incl. Artificer), 18 skills, 15 conditions, 9 species, combat actions, CC-BY-4.0 attribution
- `RULESETS` registry: `srd-5.2`, `pathfinder-2e`, `osr`, `custom`
- `get_ruleset_context(ruleset_id)` → compact dict for agent context
- `build_ruleset_prompt_context(ruleset_id)` → LLM-injectable string with SRD mechanics + required attribution
- `GET /rulesets` (public) — list known rulesets; `GET /rulesets/{id}` (auth) — full structured data

**Backend — `generate.py`**
- Adds `ruleset_context` key to NPC and loot generation context; populated by `build_ruleset_prompt_context` when `ruleset == "srd-5.2"`, empty string otherwise

**Frontend — `CampaignSetupWizard.tsx`**
- Replaces freetext ruleset `<input>` with a `<select>` of known options; selecting "Custom / Homebrew" surfaces a text input for freeform entry. Unknown stored values fall back gracefully to the custom path.

```tsx
<select value={rulesetSelectValue(settings.ruleset)} ...>
  <option value="srd-5.2">D&D 5e — SRD 5.2 (CC-BY-4.0)</option>
  <option value="pathfinder-2e">Pathfinder 2e (Paizo / ORC License)</option>
  <option value="osr">OSR / Old-School Essentials</option>
  <option value="custom">Custom / Homebrew</option>
</select>
{rulesetSelectValue(settings.ruleset) === 'custom' && <input ... />}
```

**Tests — `server/tests/test_srd.py` (new)**
- 24 tests: SRD data integrity (class/skill/condition counts), helper function behaviour, and all `/rulesets` API endpoints

body:
## Summary
This PR introduces an AutoSell feature that automatically triggers drug sales when a buyer ped is in range, eliminating the need for manual target interaction. It also refactors repetitive buyer despawn code into a reusable function.

## Key Changes
- **AutoSell Feature**: Added configurable automatic sale triggering when buyer ped is within 2.5 units for a configurable delay (default 1500ms)
  - New config option `Config.AutoSell` with `enabled` and `delay` settings
  - Target system is disabled when AutoSell is enabled
  - Added `isSaleAnimating` flag to prevent multiple simultaneous sales
  
- **Refactored Despawn Logic**: Consolidated repetitive buyer despawn code into a new `despawnBuyerPed()` function
  - Replaces multiple instances of `TaskWanderStandard()` + cleanup threads
  - Ped walks away from player (30 units) before despawning
  - Handles edge case where ped is on top of player by picking random direction
  - Cleans up `interactedPeds` table on despawn

- **State Management Improvements**:
  - Added `isSaleAnimating` flag to track active sale animations
  - Reset `interactedPeds` table in `resetSellState()` for cleaner state management
  - Added `autoSellTimer` to track delay timing for AutoSell feature

- **Code Quality**: Reduced code duplication by replacing ~8 instances of identical despawn logic with single function call

## Implementation Details
- AutoSell uses `GetGameTimer()` for precise delay timing
- Target system conditionally registers based on AutoSell enabled state
- Despawn function validates entity existence before operations
- Maintains backward compatibility - AutoSell is disabled by default

author: bbpddev
body:
## Summary
This PR adds support for OpenAI's Realtime API as an alternative to xAI's Grok Realtime API, allowing users to choose between voice providers in the admin portal.

## Key Changes

**Backend (server.py):**
- Added `OPENAI_REALTIME_BASE_URL` constant for OpenAI's realtime endpoint
- Extended `AgentConfig` model with `api_provider` (xai/openai) and `openai_model` fields
- Refactored `voice_agent_ws()` WebSocket handler to support both providers:
  - Dynamically builds connection parameters and session config based on selected provider
  - Implements event type normalization for OpenAI (maps `response.audio.*` events to xAI's `response.output_audio.*` format)
  - Maintains backward compatibility with existing xAI implementation
- Updated config endpoints (`get_agent_config`, `update_config`, `reset_config`) to persist and return provider settings

**Frontend (AdminPortal.jsx):**
- Split voice options into provider-specific lists (`XAI_VOICE_OPTIONS` and `OPENAI_VOICE_OPTIONS`)
- Added API Provider selector UI with toggle between "Grok (xAI)" and "OpenAI"
- Added OpenAI Model input field (defaults to `gpt-realtime-1.5`)
- Voice dropdown dynamically updates based on selected provider
- Updated config save/reset flows to handle new provider fields

## Implementation Details

- **Event Normalization:** OpenAI's event naming convention differs from xAI's. The backend translates OpenAI events (`response.audio.delta`, `response.audio_transcript.delta`, etc.) to xAI's format so the frontend requires no changes
- **Provider Detection:** Config is fetched at WebSocket connection time, allowing provider switching without server restart
- **Backward Compatibility:** Defaults to xAI provider if not specified, ensuring existing deployments continue working
- **Voice Switching:** When provider changes, voice automatically resets to that provider's default to prevent invalid combinations

## Summary
Add a hard post-deploy availability gate to `Deploy Channels` so the workflow fails when GitHub Pages is unavailable or the preview URL is not reachable.

## Changes
- Added `pages: read` permission in deploy workflow.
- Added `Verify preview deployment availability` step after publishing preview:
  - checks GitHub Pages site API (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages`) and fails on non-200
  - polls preview `index.html` for HTTP 200 and app shell marker (`id="app"`) with retry
  - fails workflow if preview never becomes reachable
- Documented this hard fail behavior in README deployment notes.

## Why
Previously the deployment pipeline could stay green even when preview hosting was not actually available.

## Verification
- `npm run format`
- `npm run lint`

author: asmithbot
body:
## Summary
- Updated `CSystem::Init` in `src/system.cpp` to allocate `m_mapBuffer` with stage-aware array allocation:
  - from: `new unsigned char[m_mapSize]`
  - to: `new ((CMemory::CStage*)m_mapStage, (char*)"system.cpp", 0x123) unsigned char[m_mapSize]`
- This aligns the allocation path with the game's stage allocator semantics used throughout the codebase.

## Functions improved
- Unit: `main/system`
- Function: `Init__7CSystemFv`

## Match evidence
- `Init__7CSystemFv` match improved from **65.985985%** to **66.45795%**
- Delta: **+0.471965**
- Function size remains `856` bytes
- Objdiff changed-instruction count reduced from `124` to `120`

## Plausibility rationale
- The updated code is source-plausible and consistent with existing FFCC decomp patterns where large buffers are allocated via `new[]` with `(CMemory::CStage*, file, line)` metadata.
- The change reflects likely original engine memory-management intent rather than synthetic compiler coaxing.

## Technical details
- Ghidra reference for PAL `Init__7CSystemFv` indicates `__nwa__FUlPQ27CMemory6CStagePci(..., m_mapStage, "system.cpp", 0x123)` for this allocation site.
- Using stage-aware `new[]` in decomp source produced a measurable assembly alignment gain while preserving behavior.

author: fotoetienne
body:
## Summary
- Detect existing Minion work when running `gru fix` by checking the MinionRegistry before creating a new session
- Show clear error with actionable options (attach, resume, or `--force-new`) when a Minion already exists for the issue
- Use `is_process_alive` for stale PID detection to distinguish running vs stopped Minions
- Add `--force-new` flag to bypass the check and create a new session regardless
- Add `find_by_issue` method to MinionRegistry for querying by repo+issue

## Test plan
- Added 3 unit tests for `find_by_issue`: matching minions, no match (wrong issue/repo), empty registry
- All 326 tests pass (`just test`)
- All checks pass (`just check` - fmt, clippy, test, build)

## Notes
- The duplicate check runs inside `spawn_blocking` consistent with all other registry operations in `handle_fix`
- `is_process_alive` (a single `kill(pid, 0)` syscall) is called outside `spawn_blocking` since it completes in microseconds — documented with a comment
- Both running and stopped Minions block new creation per the acceptance criteria; the error message adapts based on live process status

Fixes #183

author: deyvisgova
body:
### Motivation
- Modernize the clients and providers CRUD UX by moving create/edit into a modal and adding quick actions in the list header.
- Allow storing and searching by company name and relax required name validation to support corporate records and API autocompletion results.
- Improve search responsiveness with a debounce and return clearer backend validation and error messages for save/delete flows.

### Description
- Frontend: updated `clientes-crud.html` / `proveedores-crud.html` and corresponding `.ts` and `.css` files to introduce a modal-based create/edit form, add a `nombreEmpresa` field, add a search input with `onFiltroChange()` debounce, and tweak styles (spacing, button radius, table container scrolling, sticky headers, and modal styles).
- Frontend: replaced older DNI-only lookup with a unified `consultarDocumentoApi()` that queries DNI or RUC via `consultarApi()` and autofills either person or company fields using `autocompletarDesdeDni()` and `autocompletarDesdeRuc()`; improved client-side validation and error display and preserved API error messages when available.
- Backend: updated `ClienteController` and `ProveedorController` to include `nombre_empresa` in search and payload handling, made `nombres`/`apellidos` nullable in validation, added a `normalizarPayload()` helper to convert nullable name fields to empty strings for NOT NULL DB columns, and returned clearer error messages when operations fail.
- Model: added `nombre_empresa` to `Cliente::$fillable` so company names are persisted.

### Testing
- Ran frontend type check and build with `ng build` to validate template and TypeScript changes, which completed successfully.
- Ran backend test suite with `php artisan test` to validate controller/model behavior, which completed successfully.

author: okayu9
body:
## Summary

- Add `ToolDefinition` interface and `ToolRegistry` class for managing agent tools with risk-level gating (low/medium execute directly, high throws error)
- Add `defineTool<T>()` helper for type-safe tool creation without `any` in the registry
- Integrate tool registry with AI SDK's `tool()` and `stopWhen: stepCountIs(5)` in the agent workflow
- Fix flaky history test caused by timestamp collisions in tight loops

## Details

- `src/tools/types.ts`: Non-generic `ToolDefinition` interface + `defineTool<T>()` helper with a single contained `as` cast (safe because Zod validates input at runtime)
- `src/tools/registry.ts`: `ToolRegistry` with `register()`, `getAll()`, `toAISDKTools()` — converts to AI SDK `Tool` type using `tool<unknown, unknown>()`
- `src/agent/prompt.ts`: `buildSystemPrompt()` now renders tool descriptions with risk levels and includes medium-risk reporting instruction
- `src/agent/workflow.ts`: Creates empty registry (no tools registered yet), passes tools to `generateText()` with `stopWhen: stepCountIs(5)`

## Test plan

- [x] Registry tests: register, getAll, toAISDKTools, risk-level gating (7 tests)
- [x] Prompt tests: no-tools message, tool rendering, medium-risk instruction (7 tests)
- [x] All 38 tests pass (`bunx vitest run`)
- [x] Biome check passes (`bunx biome check .`)
- [x] TypeScript check passes (`bunx tsc --noEmit`)

author: aperim-agent
body:
## Summary

- Add `api-cors` middleware in Traefik dynamic config so CORS headers are present even on proxy-generated 502/503 responses (when the API backend is unreachable)
- Make Fastify's `@fastify/cors` conditional via `CORS_HANDLED_BY_PROXY` env var to prevent duplicate `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` headers that browsers reject
- Add `ErrorBanner` to `ConnectionDetailPage` with clear "Terminal worker unavailable" messaging when connection test or session creation fails with 502
- Add regression tests for CORS headers on 502/500 error responses and Traefik middleware verification

Closes #1904

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `docker/traefik/dynamic-config.yml.template` | Add `api-cors` middleware with `accessControlAllowOriginList`, apply to `api-router` |
| `docker-compose.traefik.yml` | Set `CORS_HANDLED_BY_PROXY=true` for API service |
| `src/api/cors.ts` | Skip `@fastify/cors` when `CORS_HANDLED_BY_PROXY` is set |
| `src/api/cors.test.ts` | Add tests for CORS on 502/500 responses (+2 tests) |
| `docker/traefik/tests/test-entrypoint.sh` | Add tests for CORS middleware presence (+2 tests) |
| `src/ui/pages/terminal/ConnectionDetailPage.tsx` | Add `ErrorBanner` with `formatMutationError()` for 502 handling |

## Root Cause

The request flow is `Client → Traefik → ModSecurity → Fastify → gRPC worker`. CORS headers were only set by `@fastify/cors` in the application layer. When a 502 originates from the proxy chain (Traefik/ModSecurity) rather than Fastify, no CORS headers are present and browsers block the response entirely.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run src/api/cors.test.ts` — 13 tests pass (2 new)
- [x] `pnpm exec vitest run tests/ui/terminal-connections.test.tsx` — 5 tests pass
- [x] `bash docker/traefik/tests/test-entrypoint.sh` — 31 tests pass (2 new)
- [ ] Deploy to staging and verify terminal connection test/session creation shows proper error message on 502
- [ ] Verify CORS headers present on proxy-generated 502 via browser DevTools

author: gunnargray-dev
body:
## What

Adds two things that make the repo welcoming to external contributors and smarter about issue management:

1. **`CONTRIBUTING.md`** — A complete contribution guide explaining how the AI works, how to open issues for Computer, branch naming conventions, code style rules, and how to talk to the AI via PR comments.

2. **`src/issue_triage.py`** — A pure-stdlib issue classification and prioritization engine. Reads GitHub issue data (JSON format), categorizes each issue as BUG / FEATURE / ENHANCEMENT / QUESTION / CHORE / UNKNOWN, computes a 1–5 priority score, and renders a ranked Markdown report. Integrated into `src/brain.py` (coming in a later PR) for automated task selection.

## Why

- The repo has no on-ramp for humans who want to collaborate or request features. CONTRIBUTING.md fixes that.
- Without triage, Computer has no systematic way to decide which issues matter most. The triage engine gives Computer a scored, ranked backlog at the start of every session.
- The `human-priority` label convention (described in CONTRIBUTING.md and weighted +3 in the triage engine) creates a direct feedback loop: humans label issues, Computer prioritizes them.

## How

**`issue_triage.py`:**
- `_classify_category()`: regex-based classifier across 5 categories; label overrides always win over text classification
- `_compute_priority()`: weighted scoring from labels (human-priority: +3, bug: +2, triage:high: +2, triage:low: -2, wontfix: -3) + category boost + comment engagement
- `triage_issues()`: main entry point — accepts raw GitHub issue dicts (both string-label and dict-label formats)
- `TriageReport.to_markdown()`: renders a ranked table with priority emoji (🔴🟠🟡🔵⚪) + category breakdown
- Supports both `comments` and `comment_count` keys (GitHub API uses both)

author: copilot
body:
When two streams were distributed across slots simultaneously, ending or switching one stream would knock out the other active stream. Three distinct bugs caused this.

## Bugs Fixed

### `stream.html` — `broadcast_selected` handler stops wrong stream
The handler stopped frame capture whenever `message.streamId !== 'camera_main'`, so activating *any* second stream in multicast mode immediately killed EUD1's ongoing camera broadcast.

```js
// Before — stops capture for ANY non-camera_main message (wrong in multicast)
else if (message.streamId !== 'camera_main' && frameCapture) { stopCapture(); }

// After — only stops when camera_main is explicitly deactivated
else if (message.streamId === 'camera_main' && message.active === false && frameCapture) { stopCapture(); }
```

### `stream.html` — `deselectStream` sends `streamId: null`
Always broadcasting `streamId: null` made it impossible for receivers to know *which* stream was stopped, causing all frame-capture to halt on any deselect event. Now sends the actual `streamId` + `active: false`.

### `stream.html` — `removeIncomingStream` leaves stale broadcast state
When a stream source ended, `streamSlotMap` was not freed and no deactivation message was sent to viewers — they kept showing the dead stream. Now cleans up the slot and broadcasts `broadcast_selected` + `stream_share` (both with `active: false`).

### `stream_share_1–15.html` — `broadcast_selected` handler + `hideStream()`
- Handler didn't check `active === false`, so deactivation messages with a non-null `streamId` never triggered `hideStream()`.
- `hideStream()` didn't reset `currentBroadcastStreamId`, allowing subsequent camera frames for a stopped stream to still render.

Both fixed: `hideStream()` now resets `currentBroadcastStreamId = null`, and the `broadcast_selected` handler gates on `data.active === false` to call it.

author: jeffin2007
body:
### Motivation

- Improve backend robustness with centralized error handling, request validation, role-based access control, and clear API responses for the demo platform.
- Add a transparent demo AI risk scoring endpoint and associated validators so the product can showcase explainable model output.
- Modernize the frontend with a proper auth flow, global state, toast notifications and reusable UI primitives to support protected routes and better UX.
- Introduce a basic GitHub Actions CI pipeline and Kubernetes manifests to standardize build/test and provide a path for demo deployment.

### Description

- Backend: added modular middleware and utilities including `asyncHandler`, `AppError`, and `apiResponse` helpers, plus global `errorHandler` and `notFoundHandler`; unified route wiring in `server.js` and made DB connectivity resilient with health endpoints.  Added `authMiddleware`, improved `roleMiddleware`, `validateRequest`, and validator modules under `validators/` for input validation.  Implemented controllers for AI (`aiController`) and upgraded `authController`, `patientController`, `doctorController`, and `prescriptionController` to use the new utilities and return consistent responses.  Added `seed/seedRoles.js` and a `seed:roles` npm script in `backend/package.json` and introduced `express-validator` to dependencies.
- Frontend: introduced `AuthContext`, `ToastContext`, and storage helpers, switched to a service-based `api` instance with 401 handling, added `ProtectedRoute` and multiple UI components (`Button`, `LoadingSpinner`, `EmptyState`, `InlineError`, `SkeletonBlock`) and hooks (`useApiRequest`, `useAuth`), plus many page refinements (Dashboard, Doctors, PatientDashboard, PatientDetails, SignIn, SelectRole).  Also updated styles and `tailwind.config.js` for the refreshed look and accessibility touches.
- CI & infra/docs: added `/.github/workflows/platform-ci-cd.yml` to run `npm ci`, `npm test`, frontend build and a Docker build on PRs and pushes to `main`; added multiple `infra/k8s` manifests (`api-gateway`, `patient-service`, demo HPA) and a large design doc `README_ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/NATIONAL_INFRASTRUCTURE_BLUEPRINT.md` describing the platform vision.
- Misc: added route files for AI and wired them into the backend; refactored many route handlers to use consistent `sendSuccess`/`sendError`; updated `backend/.env` to reference a cloud MongoDB URI placeholder (ensure secrets are set before running); added `platform-ci-cd` workflow and Docker build step for `patient-service` image.

### Testing

- No automated test suites were executed as part of this PR submission, but a CI job `platform-ci-cd` was added that will run the following on PRs and `main` pushes: backend `npm ci` and `npm test --if-present`, frontend `npm ci`, `npm test` (with `--watchAll=false`) and `npm run build`, and a Docker build for the `patient-service` image; the workflow is staged to validate future changes.
- Existing local test scripts (if any present in the repo) will be executed by the CI workflow; please ensure environment secrets (Mongo URI, Docker registry creds) are configured in CI before relying on full end-to-end runs.

body:
`image 0.25` with the `avif` feature (on by default) transitively pulls in `wasm-bindgen`, which emits imports from `__wbindgen_placeholder__` (e.g. `__wbindgen_describe`) into the WASM binary. Since Typst has no implementation for these imports, loading the plugin fails with `cannot find definition for import __wbindgen_placeholder__::__wbindgen_describe`.

## Changes

- **`crates/wasi-stub/src/lib.rs`**: Add `__wbindgen_placeholder__` to the default set of stubbed modules in `ShouldStub::default()`, alongside the existing `wasi_snapshot_preview1`.

```rust
modules: [
    (String::from("wasi_snapshot_preview1"), FunctionsToStub::All),
    (String::from("__wbindgen_placeholder__"), FunctionsToStub::All),
]
```

Users can already opt into this manually via `--stub-module __wbindgen_placeholder__`; this makes it automatic so wasm-bindgen introspection stubs are silenced without any extra flags.

- **`crates/wasi-stub/src/lib.rs` (tests)**: Added unit tests to verify the default stubbing behaviour:
  - `test_wbindgen_placeholder_stubbed_by_default` — constructs a synthetic WASM binary with a `__wbindgen_placeholder__::__wbindgen_describe` import and asserts it is stubbed out by default.
  - `test_wasi_snapshot_preview1_stubbed_by_default` — same check for the existing `wasi_snapshot_preview1` module.
  - `test_unknown_module_not_stubbed_by_default` — verifies that arbitrary unknown modules are left untouched.

author: sleyv
body:
🎯 **What:** The vulnerability fixed
The `app.static("/", BASE_DIR, index="index.html", name="root")` call allowed any file in the base directory to be served as a static asset, leading to potential directory traversal and source code exposure. The fix replaces this overly permissive route with explicitly defined `@app.get` routes that strictly serve only safe public assets (`index.html`, `icon-192.png`, `icon-512.png`). 

⚠️ **Risk:** The potential impact if left unfixed
An attacker could retrieve arbitrary files stored within the application's root directory, including sensitive files like `main.py`, `.env` files, Docker configurations, and potentially TLS certificates if the server was configured insecurely or `BASE_DIR` overlapped with sensitive storage locations.

🛡️ **Solution:** How the fix addresses the vulnerability
Instead of allowing dynamic resolution of any file path matching the URL, the routing logic has been restricted to specifically whitelist the exact files required for the PWA front-end to operate correctly. Requests to any other paths (e.g., `/main.py`) will safely return a 404 Not Found response, preventing data exposure.

author: twmb
body:
Had my main branch laying around for a few years, wrote serialization, then rewrote it to do a different approach, then decided eh this is a lot and put it down... The goal at the time was to beat hamba/avro, but to be honest, I took a look at the guts of that library and it's really good, which is another (probably bigger?) reason I put this down. Well, LLMs can help take it the rest of the way there! And coincidentally, hamba/avro is archived as of a month ago. The aim with this repo is to be fast, opt into stdlib unsafe code, but avoid dependencies and avoid the reflect2 package that is falling out of date (and was always odd to me anyway). This is faster at serializing (by a bit) but slower at deserializing (less alloc avoiding tricks we have available). This initial PR has extensive coverage (100%). More will come. The goal of this repo is NOT to support all the extensions people have in hamba's repo on top of the base avro encoding/decoding. If extensions are ever supported, they'll be in submodules.

---

Add deser.go and unsafe.go implementing deserialization and unsafe pointer-based fast paths for records, arrays, null-unions, and all primitive types. Expand schema parsing, serialization, and varint encoding. Replace ptr(x) helper with Go 1.26 new(x) syntax.

Fix an integer overflow where a crafted array/map block count of math.MinInt64 survives count = -count (since -MinInt64 == MinInt64 in two's complement), causing a SetLen panic. All four block-count consumers now guard against this.

Add adversarial tests covering length-lying strings/bytes, array count lies, MinInt64 block counts, null-union invalid indices, byte-by-byte truncation sweeps, no-aliasing verification, redecode overwrite, varint boundary values, map key length lies, alignment stress, field order mismatch, and embedded struct offset paths.

body:
## Summary
This PR adds a new API interface for inspecting the state and execution history of periodic jobs in Mosquito. It introduces observability features that track when periodic jobs are executed and provides read-only access to this metadata.

## Key Changes
- **New `Mosquito::Api::PeriodicJob` class**: Provides a read-only interface to inspect periodic job metadata, including:
  - Job name and configured interval
  - Last execution timestamp (or nil if never run)
  - Static `all` method to list all registered periodic jobs
  
- **New `Mosquito::Observability::PeriodicJob` class**: Implements observability/event publishing for periodic job execution:
  - Publishes "enqueued" events when a periodic job is executed
  - Logs execution and skip events
  - Provides publish context for event tracking
  
- **Updated `PeriodicJobRun`**: 
  - Added `observer` getter to access the observability interface
  - Calls `observer.enqueued()` when a job is executed
  - Calls `observer.skipped()` when a job is not yet due
  
- **Updated `Mosquito::Api` module**: Added `list_periodic_jobs` convenience method

## Implementation Details
- Periodic job execution timestamps are stored in the backend metadata store using the key pattern `periodic_jobs:{job_name}`
- The `last_executed_at` property returns a `Time?` object, allowing callers to distinguish between "never run" and actual execution times
- Event publishing follows the existing Mosquito observability patterns with proper context and logging
- All changes maintain backward compatibility with existing periodic job functionality

body:
### Motivation
- Add on-demand procedural world generation and caching so the game can stream large worlds without blocking the UI. 
- Prioritize simulation work around the player to keep nearby activity responsive while throttling distant updates. 
- Surface biome hints and modifier UI feedback to help users understand procedural state and editing shortcuts.

### Description
- Introduces a new `procgen` module that implements `ProcGenConfig`, `generate_world`, biome sampling, and many helper noise/placement routines, plus `find_safe_spawn` and `biome_hint_at_world` utilities. 
- Adds background procgen job queueing with `queue_procgen_job`, `ProcgenJobSpec`/`ProcgenJobResult`, a channel pair, region caching (`generated_regions`) and pruning, and logic in `app::run` to request/graft generated macro-regions and reposition the player on generation completion. 
- Adds `world_manager` module (initial macrochunk manager API) and constants for macrochunk sizes and render radii, and wires macrochunk logic into `sim` via `prioritize_chunks_for_player`, `step_selected_chunks`, `macrochunk_from_world`, and chunk-selection helpers to run high/low priority updates; the main loop now throttles low-priority ticks. 
- Updates `sim` to support stepping only selected chunks (`step_selected_chunks`) and to expose helper conversion utilities; moves the previous full-iteration `step` to call the selected-chunk variant. 
- Improves collision logic in `player::FpsController::collides` to consider material `Phase` when deciding solidity (imports `Phase`/`material`). 
- Adjusts renderer face-occlusion rules with `is_face_occluded(self_id, neighbor_id)` to avoid drawing faces when neighbor equals self and to respect translucency and some special cases. 
- UI additions: `New Procedural` button, `biome_hint` string shown near hotbar, modifier hint overlay, and new fields/actions in `UiState`/`UiActions`. 
- Miscellaneous utilities added: `floor_div`, `prune_generated_regions`, `next_missing_region_origin`, and cursor unlocking helper `should_unlock_cursor`.

### Testing
- Ran `cargo build` to ensure the project compiles after additions and refactors, and the build completed successfully. 
- Ran `cargo test` (existing test-suite) and it completed without failures. 
- Performed a basic automated smoke build-run to exercise the event loop and procgen job path; the application started and accepted UI interactions (procedural generation request path exercised) without runtime panics.

## 🚀 Major Update: Flutter Implementation, Privacy & Terms, and Build Modernization

### Overview

This PR delivers a comprehensive update to the WalkTracker project, spanning legal compliance, build and namespace modernization, IDE configuration, and the addition of a new cross-platform Flutter implementation (`walk_tracker_lite`). Together, these changes improve privacy readiness, development workflows, and platform reach while keeping the existing Kotlin Android app fully functional.

---

## 📱 New: Flutter App (`walk_tracker_lite`)

A complete cross-platform Flutter implementation has been added alongside the existing Kotlin Android app.

### Highlights

* ✨ Cross-platform support (Android + iOS)
* 🎨 Modern, responsive Flutter UI
* 📊 Core walking tracking (steps, distance, activity monitoring)
* 🗺️ Real-time GPS/location services integration
* 💾 Local persistence using SQLite/Hive
* 📈 Statistics and progress analytics
* 🧪 Includes unit and widget tests

### Project Structure

```
walk_tracker_lite/
├── lib/               # Flutter application code
├── android/           # Android-specific configs
├── ios/               # iOS-specific configs
├── test/              # Tests
├── pubspec.yaml       # Dependencies
└── README.md          # Flutter app docs
```

### Intent

* Expand platform reach to iOS without maintaining separate native codebases
* Provide a lightweight, cross-platform alternative while keeping the Kotlin app as the primary Android implementation
* Enable faster UI iteration with Flutter’s hot reload and widget ecosystem

---

## 🔐 Documentation & Legal Compliance

* Added `PRIVACY_POLICY.md` describing data handling, local device storage, Fitbit and Google integrations, and user rights.
* Added `TERMS_OF_SERVICE.md` outlining usage rights, third-party services, disclaimers, and open-source licensing.
* Updates prepare the app for Play Store and App Store distribution requirements.

---

## 🛠️ Build System & Namespace Modernization

* Renamed app namespace from `com.example.walktracker` to `com.carefuldata.walktracker` across build files, source, and ProGuard rules for consistent branding.
* Upgraded Java and Kotlin compatibility to version 17.
* Migrated Room annotation processing from `kapt` to `ksp` for improved build performance and modern tooling.
* Added support for loading Fitbit OAuth credentials from a local, gitignored `secrets.properties` file for secure API configuration.

---

## 📄 Android Manifest & OAuth Integration

* Registered a new intent filter in `AndroidManifest.xml` to handle Fitbit OAuth callbacks, enabling secure account authentication flows.

---

## 🧑‍💻 IDE & Code Style Configuration

* Added Android Studio `.idea` configuration files:

  * Kotlin/XML code style rules
  * Compiler and run configurations
  * Project metadata for consistent formatting and local setup
* Goal: reduce environment drift and ensure consistent development workflows across contributors.

---

## 📚 Documentation Improvements

* Updated `README.md` with clearer build and run instructions for:

  * Android Studio workflows
  * Command-line builds
  * Dual-app (Kotlin + Flutter) project structure

---

## 🎯 Why These Changes?

* **Cross-platform reach:** Flutter enables iOS support with a single codebase.
* **Modern tooling:** Java/Kotlin 17 + KSP improves performance and maintainability.
* **Security & compliance:** Privacy policy and terms prepare the project for store distribution and user trust.
* **Developer experience:** IDE configs and updated docs standardize setup and reduce onboarding friction.
* **Flexibility:** Kotlin app remains the primary Android implementation; Flutter provides a lighter cross-platform option.

---

## 🔄 Migration & Compatibility Notes

* No breaking changes to existing Kotlin functionality.
* Kotlin Android app continues as the main production implementation.
* `walk_tracker_lite` is an additional, independent Flutter app.
* Both apps can coexist and be versioned/released independently.

---

## 🧪 Testing Status

* Flutter app builds successfully on Android and iOS.
* Core tracking features verified in both implementations.
* Privacy policy and terms accessible from both apps.
* Existing Kotlin app functionality remains intact.

---

## 📦 Deployment Considerations

* Repository now contains two applications with separate build and release pipelines.
* Each app can follow independent versioning strategies.
* Documentation updated to reflect the dual-app architecture.

---

## 🤝 Type of Change

* ✨ New feature (adds cross-platform Flutter implementation)
* 🔧 Build and configuration updates
* 📚 Documentation and legal compliance additions

> Note: This is a substantial addition (~100k+ lines). The Flutter app provides a full alternative implementation while preserving the original Kotlin Android app as the primary Android solution.

### Descripción

Se introduce un **nuevo feature en el backend** que agrega un endpoint para obtener los tweets de un usuario específico, identificado tanto por `id` como por `username`.  
Este cambio amplía la API para brindar soporte a una funcionalidad clave del challenge: permitir que el cliente consulte todos los tweets de un usuario de forma paginada y ordenada cronológicamente, utilizando un servicio dedicado que encapsula la lógica de negocio y manteniendo controladores delgados.

La implementación sigue las convenciones existentes del proyecto (servicios, responses JSON consistentes y patrones de error), y se incluyen pruebas de integración para asegurar el comportamiento esperado.

---

### Cambios

- **Nuevo endpoint backend:**  
  - Se agrega `UserTweetsController#index` bajo la ruta `GET /api/v1/users/:id/tweets`, permitiendo consultar tweets de un usuario por su `id` o `username`. :contentReference[oaicite:0]{index=0}
- **Servicio de negocio dedicado:**  
  - Se introduce `UserTweets::Fetcher` para encapsular la extracción de parámetros, validación del usuario objetivo y consulta paginada de tweets ordenados por fecha descendente. :contentReference[oaicite:1]{index=1}
- **Vista JBuilder:**  
  - Se agrega la plantilla `index.json.jbuilder` para serializar la lista de tweets del usuario utilizando el partial de tweet existente. :contentReference[oaicite:2]{index=2}
- **Rutas actualizadas:**  
  - Se registra la ruta miembro `get :tweets, to: "user_tweets#index"` dentro de `config/routes.rb` para `users`. :contentReference[oaicite:3]{index=3}
- **Documentación OpenAPI:**  
  - Se actualiza el spec `api_v1_users.yml` con la operación `GET /api/v1/users/{id}/tweets`, incluyendo parámetros de paginación y referencias a los schemas de tweet y errores. :contentReference[oaicite:4]{index=4}
- **Tests de integración:**  
  - Se agrega `user_tweets_test.rb` con cobertura para:
    - Obtener tweets por `username`.  
    - Obtener tweets por `id`.  
    - Manejar usuario inexistente con respuesta `404` y mensaje de error. :contentReference[oaicite:5]{index=5}
- **Ajuste menor en manejador de errores:**  
  - Se elimina una línea de depuración (`binding.break`) del concern `ErrorHandling` para evitar interrupciones no deseadas en producción. :contentReference[oaicite:6]{index=6}

body:
## Summary
- **Problem:** OpenClaw sends `role: "developer"` to all `openai-completions` providers, but only native `api.openai.com` accepts it — every other backend (Qwen, DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi, Azure, proxies) returns a hard 400
- **Why it matters:** Affected models are completely unusable, not degraded — anyone self-hosting with a non-OpenAI backend hits this immediately
- **What changed:** `normalizeModelCompat` now forces `supportsDeveloperRole: false` for any `openai-completions` model whose `baseUrl` is not `api.openai.com`; model object is no longer mutated (returns clone)
- **What did NOT change:** Native OpenAI users, non-`openai-completions` providers, and models with explicit `compat` pinned to `false` are unaffected

## Change Type
- [x] Bug fix

## Scope
- [x] API / contracts

## Linked Issue/PR
- Closes #27037

## User-visible / Behavior Changes
Non-OpenAI compatible providers (Qwen, DeepSeek, Azure, proxies) no longer receive `role: developer` — requests that previously returned 400 will now succeed. No config changes required. Manual `compat: { supportsDeveloperRole: false }` workaround still works but is no longer needed.

## Security Impact
- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No

## Repro + Verification
### Environment
- Provider: any OpenAI-compatible proxy (CPA, Qwen, DeepSeek)
- Model: `qwen-3.5-plus` or equivalent

### Steps
1. Configure an `openai-completions` provider with a non-OpenAI `baseUrl`
2. Send any message
3. Observe 400: `developer is not one of ['system', 'assistant', 'user', 'tool', 'function']`

### Expected
- Request succeeds with `role: system`

### Actual (before fix)
- Hard 400 from backend

## Evidence
- [x] New tests added: Azure, generic proxy, Qwen proxy all assert `supportsDeveloperRole: false`; native `api.openai.com` asserts unchanged

## Human Verification
- Verified scenarios: native OpenAI untouched, Azure forced off, generic proxy forced off, explicit `compat: false` respected
- Edge cases checked: empty `baseUrl` (defaults to api.openai.com behavior, left unchanged), explicit `supportsDeveloperRole: true` on non-native endpoint (correctly overridden — documented in comment)
- What I did not verify: live end-to-end call against a real Qwen/DeepSeek endpoint

## Compatibility / Migration
- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No

## Failure Recovery
- Revert: `git revert` this commit
- Workaround if needed: add `compat: { supportsDeveloperRole: true }` per model in config to restore old behavior
- Watch for: any provider that genuinely accepts `developer` role but has a non-`api.openai.com` baseUrl (none known)

## Risks and Mitigations
- Risk: a future OpenAI-compatible provider that does accept `developer` role would be incorrectly forced to `system`
  - Mitigation: per-model `compat.supportsDeveloperRole: true` override remains available and is documented

## Summary

Two new skills for visual-driven ralph workflows:

### 1. `$visual-verdict` — Semantic Visual Similarity Loop
- Enforce per-iteration visual gate for visual tasks in ralph persistence mode
- Strict schema: score 0-100, verdict in `pass|revise|fail`, non-empty reasoning
- Persist structured visual feedback into canonical ralph progress ledger
- Ralph visual input flags (`-i`, `--images-dir`)

### 2. `$web-clone` — URL-Driven Website Cloning *(NEW)*
- 5-pass pipeline: **Extract > Plan > Generate > Verify > Iterate**
- Leverages Playwright MCP for DOM extraction, accessibility snapshots, and screenshots
- Composite verdict system: visual (via `$visual-verdict`) + functional + structural
- Context budget management (DOM 30KB, snapshot 20KB, total 60KB)
- State persistence compatible with `ralph-progress.json`

Curled the live MiniMax Coding Plan API (`/v1/api/openplatform/coding_plan/remains`) and compared against `internal/provider/minimax/response.go`.

**All fields are already captured.** The API response is straightforward:

### Live API Response Shape

{

}
```

### Field Coverage

| API Field | Struct Field | Status |
|-----------|-------------|--------|
| `model_remains[].start_time` | `ModelRemain.StartTime` | ✅ |
| `model_remains[].end_time` | `ModelRemain.EndTime` | ✅ |
| `model_remains[].remains_time` | `ModelRemain.RemainsTime` | ✅ |
| `model_remains[].current_interval_total_count` | `ModelRemain.CurrentIntervalTotalCount` | ✅ |
| `model_remains[].current_interval_usage_count` | `ModelRemain.CurrentIntervalUsageCount` | ✅ |
| `model_remains[].model_name` | `ModelRemain.ModelName` | ✅ |
| `base_resp.status_code` | `BaseResp.StatusCode` | ✅ |
| `base_resp.status_msg` | `BaseResp.StatusMsg` | ✅ |
| Top-level `status_code` (error shape) | `CodingPlanResponse.StatusCode` | ✅ |
| Top-level `status_msg` (error shape) | `CodingPlanResponse.StatusMsg` | ✅ |

### Changes

- Added explicit `RemainsTime` assertion to unmarshal test (was in the JSON fixture but not directly asserted)

### Rendering Review

The detail view currently renders:
- **Plan** (inferred from total count via `InferPlan`)
- **Per-model usage bars** with utilization percentage
- **Reset countdown** from `EndTime`
- **Source** label ("api_key")

**Potentially useful data not currently rendered:**
- **Absolute remaining count** (e.g., "750 / 1500 prompts remaining") — `ModelRemain` has both `CurrentIntervalUsageCount` (remaining) and `CurrentIntervalTotalCount` but `UsagePeriod` only stores a percentage (`Utilization`). Showing absolute counts would require adding `Used`/`Total`/`RemainingCount` fields to `UsagePeriod` or a similar mechanism, plus rendering changes.
- `RemainsTime` and `StartTime` are redundant with `EndTime` for display purposes (the display layer already computes countdown from `ResetsAt`).

No new rendering infrastructure is needed for the current field set. The absolute-counts enhancement would be a cross-provider feature since other providers (Cursor, Copilot, etc.) also have absolute usage data that gets collapsed to percentages.

### Motivation

- Provide a single, comprehensive design note and literature survey for an RL controller that manages counterfactual branching and branch-management actions (`branch`, `verify`, `replace`, `merge`, `switch`, `stop`, `summarise`) for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). 
- Position the proposed Counterfactual Branch-and-Verify RAG (CBV-RAG) idea against existing work and highlight the gap for a learned branch-and-verify controller under token/latency constraints.
- Supply a reproducible, NeurIPS-ready implementation and experiment blueprint to test robustness to retrieval traps, conflicting evidence, and budgeted control.

### Description

- Specifies a detailed formalization: observation/state representation (branch DAG and active pointer), discrete and parameterised action space (including `retrieve`, `verify`, `replace`, `branch`, `switch`, `merge`, `stop`, `summarise`), transition assumptions, reward decomposition, and constraint budgeting (`token`, `latency`, `branch`).
- Includes a practical implementation blueprint covering architecture, controller choices (discrete-candidate policy vs free-form tool-calling), verifier design, branch memory data structures (DAG nodes and branch objects), retriever/summariser choices, an MVP plan, full-system extensions, and a 12-week timeline with a reproducibility checklist.
- Provides a training recipe (warm-start heuristics, offline RL with cached retrieval, staged curriculum, PPO/GRPO suggestions), an experimental plan (datasets, robustness stress tests, baselines, ablations, metrics), compute estimates, and required figures/tables for publication.

author: giulio-leone
body:
## Summary

Replace `list.pop(0)` with `collections.deque.popleft()` in `FormData.add_fields()`.

## Problem

`add_fields()` uses a work-list that drains from the front via `.pop(0)` and may grow via `.extend()` when `MultiDict` entries are encountered (BFS pattern). Each `list.pop(0)` is **O(n)** because CPython must shift all remaining elements.

## Solution

Switch from `list` to `collections.deque` and use `.popleft()` for **O(1)** front removal.

## Compatibility

- `.extend()`, truthiness, and iteration are identical on `deque`
- No API surface changes; purely internal optimisation
- Zero behaviour change

## Complexity

| Operation | Before | After |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| pop front | O(n) | O(1) |
